purpose:
The pre audit Statement of Accounts for
2025/26 is included at Appendix 1 and has been
prepared in accordance with the ‘Code of Practice on Local
Authority Accounting in the
United Kingdom 2025/26’.
content:
The pre-audit Statement of Accounts for
2025/26 included in Appendix A has been prepared in accordance with
the ‘Code of Practice on Local Authority Accounting in the
United Kingdom 2025/26’.
 
For 2025/26, it is a requirement that the
accounts are certified by the Council’s Section 151 Officer
and published on the Council’s website by 30 June 2025, and
the final audited version is published by 31 January 2027. The
first of these requirements has been met. The Council is currently
in the statutory public inspection period for the 2025/26 Statement
of Accounts, running from 1 July to 11 August 2026, in accordance
with the Accounts and Audit Regulations 2015.
 
Mr Wood, Corporate Manager - Financial
Accounting (Deputy Section 151), introduced
the report. 
 
Members raised a query about the sources of
the information provided in the report.   Mr Wood
explained that this information was obtained in-house but would
provide details of the original sources outside the meeting.
 
Members raised concerns about budget
pressures, particularly with Local Government Reform (LGR) on the
horizon. Mr Dickinson stated that there are always funding
pressures in Local Government; however, this Council is in a good
position despite the flat settlement from the Government over the
next three years and higher-than-anticipated inflation. In view of
LGR, much of the Capital Programme is being accelerated where
possible. 
 
Regarding revenue, officers are looking ahead
and endeavouring to hand over the Council in a strong financial
position, as are Chelmsford and Maldon.
 
Regarding queries relating to S106 monies, Mr
Dickinson advised that a report would be coming to this Committee
later in the municipal year.
 
Cllr Rigby MOVED, and Cllr Sankey
SECONDED the recommendation in the report.
 
A vote was taken by a show of hands and
Members RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY:
 

R1.     That the Committee notes the contents
of the report.

purpose: AGS
content:
This report
presented the revised Local Code of Governance and Annual
Governance Statement (AGS) 2025-2026. The report sets out their
significance, key components, and how they are implemented within
the local government framework and seeks approval of both
documents.

approved and signed by the Chief Executive and Leader of the
Council and is approved and adopted by this Committee.

 

R.2     That the
committee approves and adopts the Local Code of Corporate
Governance as set out in Appendix B.

The Council has a
statutory duty to maintain an up-to-date Constitution under the
Local Government Act 2000. The Constitution must cover standing
orders, delegations, and a code of conduct for members; it can also
include local conditions and rules that reflect its area and how
decisions are made.
 
The Monitoring
Officer (MO) has the responsibility to ensure that the
Council’s Constitution is up to date. To facilitate this, the
Council, under Article 12 of its Constitution, establishes a
Constitution Working Group (CWG), a cross-party body that enables
the MO to consult with Members on changes necessary to maintain an
effective, up-to-date Constitution.
 
Mrs Mayhew,
Corporate Manager (Democracy & Governance) and Monitoring
Officer (BBC), reported she would
bring the CWG Work Plan back to this Committee.
 
Cllr Rigby
MOVED, and Cllr Sankey SECONDED the recommendation in
the report.
 
A vote was taken by
a show of hands and Members RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY:
 

R1.     That the committee appoints a Constitution
Working Group of 5 members, one from each political group, as set
out in the report.

content:
This report presented the annual overview of

financial year. It outlined complaint volumes, key themes,
performance against response targets, and service improvements. The
Committee was asked to consider the findings and endorse the
continued implementation of the statutory Housing Ombudsman’s
Complaint Handling Code.

was present at the meeting and reported that whilst complaint
volumes have increased, this was aligned across all Council
services.  The complaints are being
recorded more appropriately and accurately, however, the use of AI
is also generating more complaints.  Performance against response times remains strong
as does the low number of overturned stage 2 complaints. The
Council is  focusing on strengthening
and learning and ensuring development improvements are delivered
through the Housing Improvement Board.
 
With regard to the number of complaints and
the Council’s reputation, the Director of Housing explained
that it is the Council that is held to account and they would
compensate tenants in line with Ombudsman’s guidelines which
would then be recompensated by Axis. 
Increased operational meetings are being held with Axis to further
improve customer service.

Laplain SECONDED the recommendation in the report.

and  RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY:
 

R.1.    That the Committee
considers the information contained within the Housing Services
Formal Complaints Annual Report 2025/26 and endorses the continued
implementation of the Housing Ombudsman’s Complaint Handling
Code.

purpose: To approve the Domestic Abuse Policy
content:
This report sought the Committee’s
recommendation to Council for approval of a new Brentwood Domestic
Abuse Policy. The Policy provides a clear corporate framework for
how the Council will identify, respond to and support residents
affected by domestic abuse, recognising its significant impact on
victims, children, families and communities. It strengthens the
Council’s approach across housing, homelessness,
safeguarding, community safety and wider frontline services by
setting out clear roles, referral pathways, partnership
arrangements and expectations for staff.
 
Approval of the Policy will support a more
consistent, coordinated and victim-centred response to domestic
abuse, help the Council meet its relevant statutory and partnership
responsibilities, and improve confidence that residents at risk are
identified early and directed to appropriate support.
 
Members welcomed this report.
 
Mr Brace, Director of Communities and Health,
advised  Members that procedures and
training would be available for both staff and members following
the adoption of the Policy.  He also
advised that safeguarding leads for the Council are Kim Anderson,
Corporate Manager, Communities and Health and Sean Steer, Corporate
Manager, Community Safety and Safeguarding, who should be first
points of contacts for the Council.

SECONDED the recommendations in the report.

purpose:
A report to consider listing Eagle Field as an
Asset of Community Value.
content:
The Localism Act 2011 introduced the Community
Right to Bid, a new right for local people to nominate buildings or
pieces of land that they believe contribute to the social interests
or wellbeing of their local communities to be listed on a register
of Assets of Community Value (ACVs) managed by the local authority.
The Right applied to public and private property, although there
are a number of exceptions under the legislation, including private
residences.
 
Where land is listed as an ACV, if an owner of
the listed asset subsequently wishes to dispose of it, there will
be a period of time during which the asset cannot be sold, or a
qualifying lease granted or assigned (a qualifying lease is a lease
originally granted for a 25year term). This period is known as a
moratorium and would ultimately be for a period of six months. The
moratorium is intended to allow community groups the time to
develop a proposal and raise the required capital to bid for the
asset when it comes onto the open market at the end of that period.
The owner is under no obligation to accept a bid from the community
group and can sell the property to whomever they wish once the
six-month moratorium is over.
 
On the 10 March 2020 the Community and Health
Committee agreed to list Eagle Field, Kelvedon Hatch as an ACV. The
nominating body was Kelvedon Hatch Parish Council. In 2024
Brentwood Borough Council received a request from Kelvedon Hatch
Parish Council to declassify Eagle Field, Kelvedon Hatch as an
Asset of Community Value. It was agreed by the Housing Health and
Community Committee on 11 March 2024 to declassify it. On 29 June
2026 the Council received a valid nomination from Kelvedon Hatch
Parish Council (Appendix A and B) to list Eagle Field, Kelvedon
Hatch as an Asset of Community Value.
 
Mrs Anderson introduced the report.
 
Cllr Dr Barrett MOVED and Cllr Laplain
SECONDED the recommendations in the report.
 
Members had mixed views regarding listing
Eagle Field.  However, Members were
minded to protect the green space on behalf of their
residents. 
 
A vote was taken by a show of hands and it was
RESOLVED:
 
 
R.1.    That Members list the land known as
Eagle Field, Kelvedon Hatch as an Asset of Community Value as
nominated by Kelvedon Hatch Parish Council as recommended in the
Officer Assessment as set out in Appendix G.
 
 
 
[Cllr Russell declared a
pecuniary interest and left the Chamber].

purpose:
Report to write off unrecoverable debt against
former tenant accounts.
content:
In September 2023 the Housing, Health and
Community Committee approved a Former Tenant Debt Recovery Policy
to assist with the collection of all former tenant debts. In line
with this, the council are working with an external agency to
collect former tenant debts.
 
As part of this process, a number of accounts
have been identified as requiring write offs for debts where all
avenues of recovery have been exhausted, the debt is statute barred
(6 year old debt) rendering it unrecoverable for legal action, or
the debtor has passed away and there is no money in the estate to
cover the debts. This report is seeking approval to write off the
unrecoverable debt.
 
Cllr Dr Barrett MOVED and Cllr Laplain
SECONDED the recommendations in the report.

show of hands and Members RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY:

the report is presented to the Section 151 officer in conjunction
with the Chair of Finance and Future Development Committee for
approval for write off.

purpose: 2025/26 Budget Outturn Report
content:
The report gave a summary of the overall
financial outturn position for the financial year 2025/26. The key
elements of the provisional outturn are:?
 
General Fund Revenue
• The outturn position for General Fund
(GF) revenue is set out in section 2 of the report and reflects a
balanced position against the approved budget.
• During the year, there have been
several movements to and from reserves. This includes a transfer of
£3.75m to reserves in Q1, alongside further reserve
adjustments made in response to in-year pressures and to align
resources with emerging priorities.
• Taking these movements into account,
the overall financial position is expected to remain breakeven
after the application of reserves, demonstrating a managed and
planned use of reserves to support financial stability.
 
General Fund Capital
• The GF Capital position (Appendix A of
the report) shows an underspend of £4.562m against a
programme of £8.259m. This variance largely reflects slippage
within the capital programme rather than a reduction in overall
delivery, with a number of schemes delayed or reprofiled into
future years due to timing of procurement, delivery challenges and
revised project timelines. Funding will be carried forward where
appropriate to support completion of these schemes.
 
HRA Revenue
• The Housing Revenue Account (HRA)
outturn (Appendix B of the report) is detailed in Section 9 of the
report and reports a balanced budget, with a variance of
£0.575m against the original surplus budget set.
• A stronger than anticipated position
enabled a transfer of £2.230m to earmarked reserves to
support future dwelling investment.
• This position is driven largely by
accounting adjustments for depreciation, significantly lower
interest costs arising from the application of capitalised
interest, earlier than forecast funding received from Homes England
and reduced borrowing costs arising from the profiling of the
capital programme.
 
HRA Capital
• The HRA Capital position (Appendix A of
the report) is an underspend of £22.603m against a programme
of £37.025m.
 
Cllr Kendall MOVED and Cllr Munden
SECONDED the recommendation. A vote was taken by show of
hands and it was RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY.

the 2025/26 outturn position set out in the report and Appendices A
and B.

content:
The report sought approval to adopt the
revised Essex Coast Recreational disturbance Avoidance and
Mitigation Strategy (Essex Coast RAMS) and associated tariff, as
attached in (Appendix A of the report), replacing the existing
2018–2038 Strategy.
 
The Essex Coast RAMS provides a strategic
framework to mitigate the in-combination effects of residential
development on internationally designated coastal habitats. It
enables the Council, in its role as Competent Authority, to meet
its statutory duties under the Conservation of Habitats and Species
Regulations 2017(as amended).
 
The updated Strategy is supported by a
refreshed evidence base, including a new visitor survey, and
introduces significant changes to the scale of mitigation required.
Most notably, it ensures mitigation is secured for the full
lifetime of development and reflects a substantial increase in
planned housing growth across the Zone of Influence (ZOI).
 
As a result, the RAMS tariff is proposed to
increase to £476 per dwelling or qualifying unit from 1
August 2026, ensuring that the full cost of mitigation is fairly
and proportionately applied. The report also seeks approval to
withdraw the existing RAMS Supplementary Planning Document (SPD)
and replace it with a Technical Advice Note (TAN), ensuring
guidance remains current and consistent across the Essex Coast RAMS
partnership.
 
Committee members asked for a briefing on the
subject matter to gain a better understanding. 
 
Cllr Kendall MOVED and Cllr Munden
SECONDED the recommendation. A vote was taken by show of
hands and it was RESOLVED.
 
1. To approve the
revised and updated Essex Coast Recreational Avoidance and
Mitigation Strategy (Essex Coast RAMS), as set out in Appendix A of
the report, superseding the original Essex Coast RAMS (2018-2038)
document.
 
2. To approve to
apply the new RAMS tariff of £476 per new dwelling or
qualifying unit (index-linked annually) to new development from 1st
August 2026.
 
3. To approve the
withdrawal of the adopted Essex Coast RAMS Supplementary Planning
Document (SPD), noting that its content is no longer fully aligned
with the revised strategy, evidence base and tariff and requires
updating.
 
4. To agree in
principle to replace the Essex Coast RAMS SPD with an Essex Coast
RAMS Technical Advice Note (TAN), recognising that this will
provide a consistent mechanism to guide decision-making for local
authorities within the RAMS partnership area.
 
5. To agree that, in
the interim period, the draft RAMS Technical Advice Note will be
used as a material consideration in relevant planning decisions,
ensuring that the transition from SPD to TAN does not create a
policy gap, enabling ongoing compliance with the Habitats
Regulations and providing certainty that decision-making remains
robust and defensible.
topline: The Finance & Future Development Committee has decided to approve the revised Essex Coast RAMS and associated tariff, impacting housing development costs and mitigation strategies.

content:
The report sets out the context and guidelines
for developing the Corporate Plan and Budget for 2027/28. It is
intended to provide a high-level plan for the authority when
considering future service and financial decisions.
 
The report also sets out the current local and
national context that needs to be considered in the preparation of
service plans and budget proposals through the autumn.
 
For 2027/28, the budget setting process has
been strengthened to reflect audit recommendations and wider
financial governance improvement activity. This includes clearer
documentation of assumptions, stronger audit trails, improved
quality assurance, enhanced links between resources and
performance, stronger oversight of procurement-related budget
proposals and explicit consideration of CIPFA Financial Management
Code requirements.
 
The approach is intended to ensure that the
Council can demonstrate that the budget is not only balanced and
lawful, but also supported by robust evidence, transparent
assumptions, clear governance and appropriate assurance.
 
For 2027/28, the budget setting process
reflects the additional context of Local Government Reorganisation
and the expectation that this will be the final budget set under
the Council’s current arrangements. The approach therefore
places particular emphasis on ensuring that the financial position
is robust, transparent and supported by clear evidence.
 
This includes strengthened governance, audit
trail and quality assurance arrangements, alongside explicit
consideration of statutory requirements and constraints, including
the need to set a balanced and sustainable budget. This will ensure
that the Council can demonstrate that its financial plans are
prudent, compliant and capable of supporting both audit
requirements and transition to successor arrangements.

SECONDED the recommendation. A vote was taken by show of
hands and it was RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY.

Committee approves the proposed arrangement for the budget setting
process as set out in the report.

purpose:

Civil Penalties
content:
The report sought Council approval for the
Housing Enforcement Policy and Civil Penalties Policy that have
been drafted to incorporate statutory and discretionary powers
under the Renters Rights Act 2025 which is now in force. The report
sets out the main provisions of the legislation, the new
responsibilities placed on the Council and the implications for the
Council’s resources.
 
The new legislation places further
requirements on services making landlord enforcement mandatory and
protects tenants from no fault evictions. There is a short
timescale to deliver a new service, approve policies, set charges
and design the service to meet the deadline of 1 May 2026.
 
The report sets out the timetable for
implementation of the legislation and the action being taken to
ensure that the Council is ready to implement the new powers and
duties and ensure compliance with the legislation.
 
A working group formed from Members of the
Housing, Health and Community Committee will be reviewing the
Policies on 12 March 2026 and have recommended for the policies to
be approved.

Committee to agree an interim set of Fees and Charges for the Civil
Penalties Policy.
 
R3. To review

months of operation and report back to the relevant committee.

purpose:
This report sets out to measure current
banking and post office provision and access to cash in Brentwood
Borough against national standards and ascertain long term plans
for maintenance of access from central/regional Post Office and
major banks/building societies.
content:
The report presented to the Committee
outlined an assessment of current banking and Post Office provision
within Brentwood Borough, comparing local access to cash against
national standards, and identifying the long?term plans of
central/regional Post Office services and major banks/building
societies.
Following discussion, Members expressed
dissatisfaction with the level of banking and Post Office provision
and counter service across the Borough.
The Chair, Cllr Haigh, proposed the
removal of Recommendation 1 and MOVED a replacement recommendation,
which was SECONDED by Cllr Gorton. The new recommendation
was:
R1.  Request
Officers re- review the report and bring back to a future meeting
to include the items as suggested by committee and in the meantime
write a letter to the post office.
 
A vote was taken by a show of hands and it was
RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY that a:
 
R1.  Request Officers re- review the report and
bring back to a future meeting to include the items as suggested by
committee and in the meantime write a letter to the post
office.

purpose:
To agree scope of project for improvement at
Warley Depot
content:
The report sought approval for essential
improvement works at the Warley Depot following the decision not to
relocate the Council’s waste and grounds operations at the
current time. However, the existing depot required health and
safety improvements, is inefficient in its operation with severe
congestion, conflicting vehicle movements, inadequate welfare and
office facilities, and outdated drainage, hard standing and
fire-safety infrastructure.
 
To address these highlighted risks and ensure
continued statutory service delivery, the Council must consider the
recommendations in the report, including improved access, creation
of modern welfare and office accommodation and upgraded
waste-handling areas and infrastructure.
 
The report requested approval to proceed with
the proposed high-level scheme and agreement to progress designs up
to planning application stage, noting that a final detailed scheme
and cost plan will be brought back to committee later in the
year.
 
The Chair made an amendment to R1:
The Committee
confirms that the Warley Depot will remain the operational base for
Waste and Grounds Service for Brentwood Borough Council and will
not be pursuing alternative sites. 
 
Cllr Barrett MOVED and Cllr Davies
SECONDED the recommendations. A vote was taken by show of
hands and it was RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY:
 
R1. The Committee
confirms that the Warley Depot will remain the operational base for
Waste and Grounds Service for Brentwood Borough Council and will
not be pursuing alternative sites. 
 
R2. That the
high-level proposals for the improvements required at the Warley
Depot site in Appendix B are approved
 
R3. That delegated
authority is granted to the Director of Assets and Investments in
consultation with the Chair of the Asset, Projects and Strategy
Committee to carry out the next phase of design, conclude necessary
surveys and the development of a planning application with
supporting detailed cost plan which will be presented to a future
committee for approval.
topline: The Assets, Projects & Strategy Committee has decided to approve essential improvement works at the Warley Depot for the Council's waste and grounds operations.

purpose:
Additional funding request for variation of
works
content:
The report sought approval for additional
essential works to be added to the Brentwood Centre Phase One pool
refurbishment programme, following intrusive surveys and strip-out,
additional works have been identified by the leisure
operator’s contractor, this includes end-of-life pipework,
significant roof deterioration, and the need for replacement of the
pool viewing area and external glazing.
 
Completing these works at this time, while the
pool closures are already planned, will avoid a future second
closure, reduce disruption for customers and operator, whilst
preventing escalating repair costs. The revised works require a
budget increase of £495,786, bringing the total project value
to £1,519,786, and will extend the project programme by
approximately three weeks to 19 June 2026. Committee approval was
requested to incorporate the additional works into the contract
variation and to delegate authority to the Director of Assets &
Investments to finalise contractual adjustments.
 
The Chair thanked Officers for their proactive
approach and work on this project.
 
Cllr Barrett MOVED and Cllr Davies
SECONDED the recommendations. A vote was taken by show of
hands and it was RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY:
 
R1. That the
additional identified works up to a value of £495,786 as
outlined in the report are approved to be included in the pool
refurbishment works programme for the Brentwood Centre.
 
R2. That the budget
for the additional works of £495,786 is funded from:
• bringing forward
£242,189 from the main build into this element of the
project;
• reduce the
£25,000,000 main build budget by £242,189 to
£24,757,811; and
• increase in the
budget for the Brentwood Centre Phase One pool refurbishment
programme by £253,597 .
 
R3. That delegated
authority is granted to the Director of Assets and Investment
to;
(i) Include the identified
work packages and the final contract sum of £1,519,786 in the
deed of variation to the original Leisure Management Agreement with
Everyone Active.
topline: The Assets, Projects & Strategy Committee has decided to approve additional essential works for the Brentwood Centre Phase One pool refurbishment programme.

purpose:
Project approval for feasibility to develop a
wider scheme
content:
The report provided updates on progress with
the Baytree Centre redevelopment and sought approval to proceed
with the next stages of the revised three-phase delivery approach.
Phase 1 High Street and public realm improvements have been
implemented using UKSPF funding, with further town-centre
wayfinding and street furniture enhancements scheduled for
installation in 2026. Phase 2 continues to advance, with design
development for the Baytree entrance and heritage chapel area
progressing subject to finalisation of the headlease surrender and
within the approved £1.3m budget. The report also outlined
the proposed procurement of a Development Manager to lead the
feasibility, design and commercial modelling for Phase 3, enabling
the Council to evaluate a deliverable, viable mixed-use
redevelopment scheme.
 
Cllr Barrett MOVED and Cllr Davies
SECONDED the recommendations. A vote was taken by show of
hands and it was RESOLVED UNANIMOUSLY:
 
R1. That members
note the update on progress with the Public Realm Phase of the
Baytree Project as detailed in this report.
 
R2. That members
note the next steps for the development of the Baytree centre
(Phase 3) which is the production of a feasibility report including
the workstreams outlined in 1.13 of this report
 
R3. That delegated
authority is granted to the Director of Assets and Investment in
consultation with the Chair of Assets, Projects and Strategy
Committee, to procure the feasibility report outlined in R2 which
will be presented to a future committee meeting for approval and
recommendations for next steps.

purpose:
2026/27 Budget report with MTFS to
2029/30
content:
The report and appendices set out all the
relevant information in support of the Council’s Budget for
General Fund services and Council Tax for 2026/27, together with
financial forecast information through to 2028/29.
 
Also included is information on the Housing
Revenue Account (HRA) budget for 2026/27 and the Capital Programme
2026/27 to 2029/30. The report summarised the detailed service
budgets, together with known adjustments including the impact of
the provisional central government grant funding. The key elements
of the proposed budget are:
 
General Fund
1) A proposed 2.99% increase in Council Tax
for 2026/27 for Brentwood Borough Council services.
2) Set aside Earmarked Reserves to appropriate
balances to mitigate future financial risk and build up in-borough
regeneration.
3) There is continued uncertainty of local
government financing.
4) The budget will be balanced in 2026/27 to
2028/29, with surpluses forecast for each year of the Medium-Term
Financial Strategy (MTFS).
 
Housing Revenue Account
1) A surplus is forecast for 2025/26 and
2028/29 but deficits in 2026/27 and 2027/28, resulting in an
overall decrease in HRA reserves.
2) There will be a drawdown from reserves to
pay for the deficit in 2026/27 of £338k.
3) Proposed increase in rents of 4.8% from 6
April 2026.
4) Continued investment in the delivery of
Decent Homes and development of Housing within the Borough.
5) Significant investment in the Strategic
Housing Delivery Programme ensuring the 30-year business plan is
sustainable.
 
Capital
1) Total capital investment of £6.14m
(General Fund) and £42.49m (HRA) in 2026/27.
2) Subsequent investment of £34.09m
(General Fund) and £26.85m (HRA) from 2027-30.

purpose:
To approve the Council's response to questions
raised by the Secretary of State on the content of the draft
Structural Change Order (SCO).
content:
The report considered and endorsed a proposed
response to the seven questions raised by the Ministry of Housing,
Communities and Local Government (MHCLG), in correspondence dated
16 January 2026, to inform the drafting of the Structural Changes
Order (SCO) that will be used to implement Local Government
Reorganisation in Greater Essex.
 
Due to the timescale set by the MHCLG and with
the agreement of the Monitoring Officer this item was being
presented as an urgent item to facilitate a response by the 17
February 2026 deadline.
 
Cllrs Russell and
Barber stated that, although they did not support Local Government
Reorganisation, they agreed to vote in favour of the recommendation
so as not to delay the process.
 
Cllr Aspinell MOVED and Cllr Barrett
SECONDED the recommendations in the report. A vote was taken
on a show of hands and it was RESOLVED
UNANIMOUSLY:
 
That the Council
approves to delegate authority to the Chief Executive to submit the
final response to the MHCLG - Structural Change Order (SCO) as set
out in Appendix B to the report, subject to any changes agreed in
consultation with the Leader of the Council and the opposition
Leaders prior to the 17th February deadline.
topline: The Council has decided to approve recommendations for the drafting of the Structural Changes Order for Local Government Reorganisation in Greater Essex.

purpose:
To update Members on the latest position in
respect of Local Government Reorganisation
content:
Local Government Reorganisation (LGR) will see
the abolition of all existing local authorities in Greater Essex
and the creation of entirely new unitary authorities. Essex
authorities have been working collaboratively resulting in the
production of 4 distinct reorganisation proposals that are based on
differing configurations. Brentwood Borough Council endorsed the 5
Unitary Authority proposal at the meeting of Full Council on 15
September 2025.  All 4 proposals were submitted to Government on 26 September
2025.
 
The report provided an update
on LGR and focuses on activity that has occurred since 15 September
2025, specifically:
• Launch of MHCLG
consultation
• LGR timeline
• Surrey Local Government
Reorganisation
• Council activity
relating to LGR
 
Since the report was prepared the government has made
an announcement regarding devolution that impacts Greater Essex as
well as Hampshire and the Solent, Norfolk and Suffolk, and Sussex
and Brighton.
 
On 4 December, the Government announced it is minded
to postpone the Mayoral election in Greater Essex, originally
scheduled for May 2026, to May 2028.  The rational given for
this was that the government wants to make sure strong foundations
are in place ahead of devolution, allowing time for areas to
complete the reorganisation process before Mayors take
office.
 
The Council is working collectively with councils
across Greater Essex to understand the implications of this new
timetable and what it means for the region.  Future updates on
this matter will be reported alongside the proposed quarterly LGR
update to the Assets, Projects and Strategy Committee.
 
Cllr Aspinell MOVED and Cllr Barrett
SECONDED the recommendations in the report. A vote was taken
on a show of hands and it was RESOLVED:
 
R1. That Council
notes the LGR activity undertaken since 15 September 2025 to date
and note that a quarterly LGR report including a risk register be
made to the Assets, Projects and Strategy Committee.
 
R2. That Council
delegate authority to the Strategic Director responsible for Policy
and Transformation, in consultation with the Leader of the Council,
to submit a response to the MHCLG consultation on local government
reorganisation in Essex, Southend-on-Sea and Thurrock, which aligns
with the Full Council decision made on 15 September 2025 to support
the 5 Unitary Authority proposal.
topline: The Council has decided to approve recommendations for the Local Government Reorganisation in Greater Essex, supporting the creation of new unitary authorities.

purpose:
To note the 2023/24 Infrastructure Funding
Statement
content:
The report provided an update on Brentwood
Borough Council’s Infrastructure Funding Statement (IFS) for
the financial year 2023/24. The update presented reflected a
refined picture of planning obligations and infrastructure
delivery. These changes had been made following a collaborative
review between Planning and Finance officers, which had enabled the
identification of previously unaccounted data.
 
These enhancements ensured that reporting
better aligns with regulatory requirements and provides Members and
the public with a clearer picture of how planning obligations are
being used to support local infrastructure and community needs.
 
It is important to note that these changes do
not indicate a shift in policy or delivery priorities, but rather a
minor refinement of the data to ensure transparency and
accountability.
 
A Committee member requested that training or
briefing be provided to help Members better understand the data and
background information ahead of future Infrastructure Funding
Statement (IFS) reports being presented to the Committee.
A query was raised
regarding further detail on the Section 106 contribution for 16
Westwood Avenue. The Director of Place agreed to investigate this
outside of the meeting and provide an update.
Committee members
also sought clarification on the distinction between
“Maintenance” and “Long-Term Maintenance.”
The Director of Place confirmed that a response would be provided
offline.
 
Cllr Naylor MOVED and Cllr Gorton
SECONDED the recommendation in the report. A vote was taken
by a show of hands and it was RESOLVED
UNANIMOUSLY:
 
To note the updated Infrastructure Funding
Statement 2023/2024.
topline: The Scrutiny, Performance and Standards Committee has decided to approve recommendations for the updated Infrastructure Funding Statement 2023/2024.
